proof_summary: Lucas-type binomial congruences pair the summands at indices differing by \(p\), proving that both Hankel matrices vanish modulo \(p\) strictly beyond the anti-diagonal; the boundary evaluations are \(a(p-1)=1\) and \(c(p-1)=(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Hence only the reversal permutation contributes to each determinant, and its sign \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) gives the first result while canceling the anti-diagonal product’s identical sign in the second.
